slices.title: Carry the host's out:// reply-channel contract and in-process-builtins facts in the read and bash surfaces
slices.done_when: One `bun sandbox/sandbox.ts run --repo <PR checkout> /tmp/c10-surface.json <model>` exits 0 and the delta extracted from its c10-surface.requests.jsonl into /tmp/c10-read.txt and /tmp/c10-bash.txt holds the two prescribed sentences verbatim (no `out://` on the `Supported URLs:` line, no `b2sum` and no `In-process builtins, ahead of PATH:`), with every other line of both surfaces and both `tool://` index blocks unchanged and each `upstream:` header naming the published host version the facts were re-checked against at PR time (its lgit commit adds the `## [Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry).

open_points.point: Whether the two `upstream` headers take the newly compared host sources as well as the new version, or only the version: `docs/extensions.md:286` defines the field as the version *and* the sources the text was checked against, while 范围边界 says only that the header is 更新到实施时发布版 and names `out-protocol.ts` and the `shellBuiltins` chain as the sources compared.
open_points.input: The two header lines after the change, `upstream: pi-coding-agent@<published> …`, in agent/extensions/tool-topics/SURFACE-read.md:3 and SURFACE-bash.md:3.
outputs: `upstream: pi-coding-agent@18.20.x src/prompts/tools/read.md, src/tools/read.ts` — version bumped, source list untouched
`… src/prompts/tools/read.md, src/tools/read.ts, src/internal-urls/out-protocol.ts` — the checked `out://` source added

the bash header, with or without `crates/pi-natives/src/shell.rs shell_builtins` / `crates/pi-shell/src/tools/mod.rs builtins` / `crates/pi-builtins/src/extras.rs` appended to `src/prompts/tools/bash.md, src/tools/bash.ts`
open_points.producer: agent/extensions/tool-topics/SURFACE-read.md:3 and agent/extensions/tool-topics/SURFACE-bash.md:3 author the field; its contract is docs/extensions.md:286
open_points.searched: grep `upstream` over docs/, agent/, ci/ (no CI or test asserts the value: ci/tool-topics-catalog.test.ts only requires a one-line non-empty field and catalog.problems empty); docs/extensions.md:286, docs/operations.md:191 (Upgrade and maintenance notes item 4), acceptance row 7

open_points.point: The prescribed read sentence makes the reply channel's availability a property of the session kind ('in the interactive TUI only (print, RPC and ACP sessions, and subagents, refuse it)'), but the host decides it from `outEnabled`: an explicitly configured `out.enabled` wins over `tuiTranscript` in either direction, so the claim is only the unset default; subagents are refused unconditionally.
open_points.input: An omp session with `out.enabled` configured true in print/RPC mode (or false in the interactive TUI), and a model call writing Markdown to `out://` through `write out://` or `cmd > out://`.
outputs: the write is accepted (`Shown to the user.`) although the surface says print, RPC and ACP sessions refuse it
the write is refused (`out:// is off in this session …`) in the interactive TUI although the surface says that is where it works
the sentence as prescribed is correct because the setting is unset on the machines in scope
open_points.producer: node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/src/internal-urls/out-protocol.ts:41-47 (`outRepliesActive` returns `cfgOutEnabled` when configured, otherwise `tuiTranscript`) and :53-59 (`refusal` checks `taskDepth` first); the setting is registered at node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/src/tools/settings.ts:952-963, set by `omp config` or the settings files
open_points.searched: grep -rn 'out\.enabled|outReplies' over agent/, docs/, ci/, sandbox/ (no hit — omp-config neither sets nor documents the setting); host src/internal-urls/out-protocol.ts, src/tools/settings.ts, src/prompts/internal-urls/out.md

open_points.point: Row 1's Expect accepts a `run` exit 0 that came from `untested`, while its command chain then needs a recorded model request: an untested run that made no request leaves c10-surface.requests.jsonl empty, so the extraction and both greps fail and the row exits 1 — the row states its acceptance two ways.
open_points.input: `bun sandbox/sandbox.ts run --repo <PR checkout> /tmp/c10-surface.json <a model id omp does not know>` → driver.js `untested`, `run` exit 0, empty evidence.
outputs: row 1 passes on the `run` exit alone (Expect read as pass-or-untested), leaving the read surface unobserved
row 1 exits 1 with an empty /tmp/c10-read.txt (command read literally), so the run must be repeated with another model
open_points.producer: sandbox/driver.ts:265-268 (`Model "…" not found` → `untested`), sandbox/driver.ts:311-312 (requests.jsonl written empty before the session starts), sandbox/sandbox.ts:274 (`run` exits 0 for pass or untested)
open_points.searched: sandbox/driver.ts (classify, evidence writes), sandbox/sandbox.ts (matrix/resultKind), sandbox/README.md「Scenarios and the RPC driver」result table and recorder section

gate_gaps.row: 3 — 覆盖 结果 3 [保持]：两份说明的其余条款与 topic 索引仍在
gate_gaps.input: /tmp/c10-read.txt from the row-1 run: its first `grep -qF '[FILENAME#TAG] snapshot header'` can never match because the unchanged sentence reads `copy the returned `[FILENAME#TAG]` snapshot header` (a backtick sits between `]` and ` snapshot`), so the && chain stops there and row 3 exits 1 whatever the change is; measured on the untouched file: `grep -c -F '[FILENAME#TAG] snapshot header'` → 0, `grep -c -F '[FILENAME#TAG]` snapshot header'` → 1, and a full simulation of rows 1-5 against the prescribed text gives row 3 exit 1 with the other four greps matching. The clause would be observed by the pattern with the backtick.

gate_gaps.row: 预期结果 1 — the two write transports and the availability range (行 1 only observes the channel phrase and `up to 64 KiB`)
gate_gaps.input: /tmp/c10-read.txt grepped for `write out://`, `cmd > out://`, `in the interactive TUI only` and `subagents, refuse it`: no acceptance row runs any of these, so a sentence naming neither transport and no session range still passes rows 1 and 4.

gate_gaps.row: 预期结果 2 — 代表性名字 (行 2 observes the property phrase, the switch and `type -t <name>` only)
gate_gaps.input: /tmp/c10-bash.txt grepped for `awk`, `sed`, `rg`, `jq`, `sort`, `xargs`: no row greps a representative name, so a sentence that states the property but lists no name still passes rows 2 and 5.

gate_gaps.row: 7 — 卫生：两份文件的 `upstream` 已随本次核对更新
gate_gaps.input: The checkout as it stands (SURFACE-read.md `upstream: pi-coding-agent@18.13.2 …`, SURFACE-bash.md `…@18.14.0 …`) run through row 7's command as written in body.md: the `\(13\.2\|14\.0\)` escape makes ripgrep match the literal `18.13.2|14.0`, which never occurs, so `! rg -q` exits 0 and the row passes without bumping anything (measured: exit 1 from `rg -q` on the unchanged files); with the pipe unescaped it would still accept any other value, e.g. an unpublished `@18.13.3` (measured: exit 1 from `rg -q`, row passes).
